summary: Residency validation headers misrouted by edge proxy causing intermittent p95 latency variance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent p95 latency spikes for requests that were expected to remain within eu-west residency. Traffic appears to be routed to us-east for a subset of requests causing additional cross-region hop and TLS handshake.

Impact:
- Elevated p95 latency for some inference calls (from ~90ms to ~420ms) observed by customer for ~15% of requests during spike window.
- Customer (Acme Health) is enterprise and requires EU-only residency for PHI-related workloads.

Environment:
- Hosted API (production)
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream
- Customer pinned region policy: residency=eu-west, strict=true

Steps to reproduce (as performed by CS):
1) Customer issues 10k prediction calls over 10 minutes from EU region IPs to API endpoint with residency header X-Region-Pin: eu-west.
2) Observe traced requests where ~1.5k requests include an additional edge-proxy hop and egress to us-east.
3) p95 latency for affected traces jumps to ~400-450ms (observed in customer logs and APM traces).

Observed behavior:
- Some requests include malformed or duplicated residency headers after the edge-proxy layer (example header set included X-Region-Pin: eu-west; X-Forwarded-Region: us-east).
- Upstream routing selects us-east due to header precedence rules in edge-proxy (recent config change suspected).

Expected behavior:
- Residency pin header must be honored and validated at the first stable point (edge-proxy) and not overwritten or misinterpreted by additional proxy layers.

Logs / trace examples:
- Trace ID: 0a1b2c3d-res-412007-01 (affected)
- Trace ID: 9f8e7d6c-res-412007-02 (correct eu-west path)
- Snapshot link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/edge-residency?var-trace=0a1b2c3d-res-412007-01

Initial request from customer received at 2026-03-12T14:03:12Z. First alerting from customer to support: 2026-03-12T14:18Z.
comments: 2026-03-12T14:22Z - Support (Asha): Acknowledged. Opening investigation with SRE and Edge team. Asking for request IDs and sample payloads.
2026-03-12T15:01Z - SRE (Diego): I see a spike in cross-region egress from edge-proxy group edge-prod-7 between 14:00-14:30Z. Collecting proxy logs and header dumps.

2026-03-12T16:10Z - Edge Eng (Marta): We deployed a header-normalization patch yesterday to canonicalize region headers. Investigating whether it introduced precedence inversion for X-Region-Pin vs X-Forwarded-Region.
2026-03-12T18:40Z - Support (Asha): Customer confirmed 13% of requests still show us-east in APM. Providing set of trace IDs and customer logs to eng.

2026-03-13T09:05Z - Diego: Found a race where two proxy layers applied header rewrite. Second layer lacked logic to prefer strict residency header and fell back to geo-IP region. Patch ready to ensure strict header wins.

2026-03-13T11:20Z - Support (Asha): Communicated temporary mitigation: set header X-Force-Region: true at edge (workaround) and reduced p95 to expected levels for 30 minutes during test window. Customer is testing in their next window.
2026-03-13T14:02Z - Customer (Acme Health): Confirmed default case for 99% of traffic is restored, will monitor for 24 hours before we close. Asked for documentation on header precedence.
investigation_notes: Edge-proxy header-normalization patch (deployed 2026-03-11) introduced header rewrite order change where X-Forwarded-Region could overwrite X-Region-Pin when present and strict flag was not propagated.
Observed duplicated headers when requests traverse CDN -> edge-proxy -> auth-proxy chain. auth-proxy did not drop legacy X-Forwarded-Region headers.
Traffic analysis: 15% of affected requests originated from customers behind legacy CDN nodes returning X-Forwarded-Region=us-east in initial request (geo-IP mismatch).
Temporary mitigation applied: added explicit check to edge-proxy to enforce X-Region-Pin precedence and log resync events. Confirmed p95 drop in staging and applied hotfix to edge-prod-7.
Next steps: patch auth-proxy to sanitize forwarded region headers; add automated regression test for header precedence; update residency runbook with header precedence diagram.
root_cause: Header-precedence regression introduced by header-normalization patch: a secondary proxy layer erroneously overwrote the strict residency header with a geo-IP-derived forwarded-region header leading to cross-region routing for a subset of requests.
resolution: Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy group (edge-prod-7) 2026-03-13T09:30Z enforcing strict X-Region-Pin precedence and sanitizing X-Forwarded-Region. Workaround communicated: customers can set X-Force-Region: true until auth-proxy patch is released. Auth-proxy patch scheduled for 2026-03-14 rollout.
postmortem_tasks: ENG-2346 - Add unit/integration tests for header precedence in proxy chain
OPS-889 - Roll out auth-proxy header sanitization to all edge regions
DOCS-501 - Update residency header precedence doc and customer KB article
resolution_status: Fix deployed to affected edge cluster and auth-proxy patch scheduled, customer monitoring before closure
